title: Subcellular Euclidean distance measurements with multicolor fluorescence localization imaging in cultured cells
protocol: Measure intra-kinetochore Delta Euclidian distances between two fluorescently-labeled kinetochore markers.
Measure intra-kinetochore Delta Euclidian distances between three fluorescently-labeled kinetochore markers.
Measure intra-kinetochore Delta Euclidian distance between two fluorescently-labeled kinetochore markers at kinetochores positive and negative for a third fluorescently-labeled kinetochore marker.
Quantify kinetochore marker intensity.
Sub-culture human HTERT-immortalized retinal pigment epithelial (hTERT RPE1) cells.
Use standard protocols for culturing hTERT RPE1 cells.
Acquire necessary media and reagents for cell culture.
Discard the media in which hTERT RPE1 cells are grown.
Wash the T25 flask bottom with 5 mL PBS and discard the PBS.
Add 1 mL 0.05% Trypsin EDTA to the T25 flask.
Place the flask in the incubator for 3 min or until the cells are floating in the solution.
Add 5 mL supplemented DMEM/F-12 to a new T25 flask and label it with date, cell passage, name, and cell line.
Once the cells become detached, add 4 mL supplemented DMEM/F-12 media and gently mix by pipetting.
For maintenance, add 1/10 of the cell suspension (0.5 mL) to the new T25 flask and return it to the incubator.
Add a sterile coverslip to the well of a 6-well plate.
Add 2 mL of supplemented DMEM/F-12 to the well containing the cover slip.
Add 500 μL of the cell suspension to the well.
Prepare a T75 flask by adding 15 mL supplemented DMEM/F-12 and 1.5 mL cell suspension.
Grow the cells for two days in the T75 flask.
Discard the media from the T75 flask and wash with 10 mL PBS, then discard the PBS.
Add 2 mL trypsin-EDTA to the flask and incubate for 2 min or until cells have detached.
Add 8 mL of supplemented DMEM/F-12 media to the flask and gently mix by pipetting.
Transfer the cell suspension to a 15mL falcon tube and centrifuge for 5 min at 1200 rpm.
Discard the supernatant from the cell pellet in the 15mL falcon tube.
Re-suspend the cell pellet in 10 mL freezing medium consisting of 10% DMSO, 17% FBS and 73% non-supplemented DMEM/F-12.
Add 1 mL of the cell suspension in freezing media to a cryotube.
Place the cryotube in a freezing container to cool at around 1°C/min.
Store the cryotube at -80°C for about 24 h.
Transfer the cryotube from -80°C to liquid nitrogen storage on the following day.
Prepare PTEMF (fixation solution) - 4% paraformaldehyde, 0.2% Triton X-100, 10 mM EGTA (pH = 7), 20 mM Pipes (pH = 6.8), 1 mM MgCl2, and double distilled water.
Gently discard the media with Pasteur pipette without touching the cells on the coverslip.
Add PTEMF to the well such that it covers the cover slip with cells, about 2 mL.
Incubate for 10 min at 20°C–26°C.
Prepare 3% Bovine Serum Albumin (BSA) in PBS solution during incubation time.
Add BSA powder to PBS and let it dissolve.
Discard PTEMF in a bottle for toxic waste using a Pasteur pipette.
With a Pasteur pipette, add PBS enough to cover the coverslip (about 1.5 mL).
Incubate for 5 min at 20°C–26°C.
Discard the first PBS wash in the bottle for toxic waste and add fresh PBS as before.
Incubate for 5 min at 20°C–26°C.
Discard the PBS in non-toxic waste container.
Add fresh PBS to cover the coverslip (~1.5 mL) and incubate for 5 min at 20°C–26°C.
Add 3% BSA in PBS, such that it covers the cover slip (~1.5 mL).
Incubate for 30 min at 20°C–26°C.
Cut a square of thick filter paper to fit into a 15 cm diameter plastic tissue culture dish.
Wet the filter paper with tap water and place it in the dish.
Cover the filter paper with a piece of parafilm.
Dilute the primary antibody in 3% BSA in PBS to obtain the working dilution recommended for immunofluorescence immediately before the blocking time is over.
Vortex the mixture containing all primary antibodies.
Place 100 μL of the antibody mix on parafilm in the “antibody incubation chamber”.
Carefully remove the cover slip from the 6-well plate using forceps, holding near the edges.
Discard liquid by tapping the edge of the cover slip onto a tissue while holding it vertical.
Place the cover slip with cells facing down on top of the antibody mix drop.
Close the 15 cm dish ensuring cells face down in the chamber.
Incubate for 1 hour at 20°C–26°C.
Cut a piece of parafilm and place it on top of a 6-well plate lid.
Carefully remove the cover slip from the antibody incubation chamber using forceps, holding it horizontally to discard liquid.
Place the cover slip with cells facing up onto the parafilm.
Add approximately 1 mL PBS with a Pasteur pipette and incubate for 5 minutes.
Discard the PBS with a Pasteur pipette or aspirator at minimum speed.
Repeat the washing procedure three times.
Do not discard PBS after the last wash.
Wipe the parafilm in the “antibody incubation chamber” with a tissue to remove any remaining primary antibody mix liquid.
Dilute secondary antibodies in 3% BSA in PBS to the same working dilution, creating an equal mixture.
Vortex the diluted secondary antibody mixture.
Place a 100 μL of the antibody mix in a drop on the parafilm in the “antibody incubation chamber”.
With forceps carefully take the cover slip out of the 6-well plate, holding it near the edges.
Discard the liquid by holding the cover slip vertical and tapping the edge onto a tissue.
Place the cover slip on top of the liquid drop in the “antibody incubation chamber”.
Close the 15 cm dish.
Cover the dish with foil to prevent bleaching of the fluorescence.
Incubate for 30 min at 20°C–26°C.
Wash the coverslip by following steps xi to xiii.
Clean a microscope slide with a piece of tissue and label the slide appropriately.
Add a drop of VectaShield in the middle of the microscope slide (about 20 μL).
With forceps carefully take the cover slip out of the 6-well plate, holding it near the edges.
Discard the liquid by holding the cover slip vertical and tapping the edge onto a tissue.
Place the cover slip on top of the VectaShield drop.
Seal the cover slip to the microscope slide by applying nail varnish to the edges.
Cover the slides with opaque box or foil.
Leave horizontally to dry for 1–2 h at 20°C–26°C or for about 12 h at 4°C.
Keep the slides in microscope slides box at 4°C when not in use.
Take a 12 micrometer unit z-stack, at 100 nm z-step intervals (121 images), aiming for one or two interphase cells in the center of the field of view.
Choose the z sampling such that it is Nyquist sampling or lower.
Take a dataset of 10 to 15 images of different cells for a given day of imaging.
Create a jobset file by typing jS_Name = kitGUI in the Command window.
Set up parameters for ACS analysis using the GUI that opens when creating the jobset.
Save the analysis parameters in the specified format: jS_expN_DateofImaging_ACS, replacing N with an experiment number and DateofImaging with the actual date of imaging.
Click on Select directory.
Select the folder that contains ACS images and click on Select Folder.
In the Available movies window, select the image stacks for ACS correction by clicking with left mouse button on the stack.
Add full size of selected image stacks to the bottom of the list in the ROIs window.
Repeat steps ii. and iii. until all ACS images are added to the ROIs window.
Process setup.
Select Chromatic Shift from the Process type drop down menu.
Pick the fluorophore channel with the best signal in the CS channel.
Set the detection in NCS channels with kinetochore marker to :Neighbor.
Set the refinement option to :MMF.
Use the :Circle option for ACS processing due to the absence of a metaphase plate in interphase cells.
Select Channel2 (CenpA-A647) as the CS channel.
Identify Channel1 (CenpA-A488) and Channel3 (CenpA-A561) as NCS channels.
Type jS_Name = kitGUI in the Command window to open the GUI for sample analysis.
Set up the sample analysis using the provided figures as a guide if the GUI does not fully display on Windows OS.

Name the jobset according to the format: jS_expN_DateOfImaging_ProteinsInChannelOrder_Treatment. For example, name it jS_exp1_13042020_Nnf1CenpCNdc80N_DMSO for hTERT RPE1 cells stained with anti-Nnf1, anti-CenpC and anti-Ndc80 N-terminus primary antibodies labeled with Alexa 488-, Alexa 561-, and Alexa 647-conjugated secondary antibodies respectively.
Select the folder that contains the Sample images.
Click on Select Folder.
Make sure the path of the selected folder is visible next to the Select directory button.
Load all files within the selected folder in the Available movies window.
Optional: Click on Open existing jobset and load a previously saved jobset if available.
Select all movies to be used for Sample analysis.
Add cells in the order corresponding to raw image numbering.
Click on Add Crop to facilitate spot tracking of the sample.
Open a figure with a maximum Z projection of the image stack.
Make a rectangle around the mitotic cell including some background using the Add ROI button.
Choose a coordinate system (CS) channel based on robust kinetochore localization and consistent signal across experiments.
Set the detection in non-coordinate system (NCS) channels to :Neighbor.
Set refinement in NCS channels to :MMF.
Leave detection as :None for channels with no staining or kinetochore marker.
Leave refinement as :None for channels with no staining or kinetochore marker.
Do not change spot detection and refinement options for human cells unless there is an issue.
Check the box next to Provide chromatic shift correction.
Load the ACS jobset created in step 3 into the appropriate fields based on the number of channels.
For two channels, click on the field under Jobset positioned on the right of the used channel pair (i.e., channel vector 1-2).
For three channels, load the ACS jobset into all jobset fields (1-2; 1-3; 2-3).
Enter :25 for Min spot intensity (% of max) to consider only chromatic shift spots that have an intensity which is 25% or higher of the maximum image intensity.
Discard very weak intensity spots using the value set for Min spot intensity.
Enter :0.75 for Min spot separation to discard ACS spots that are closer than 0.75 μm.
Filter background and overlapping spots based on the kinetochore sister-sister pair distance at rest (no force applied) being 0.75 μm.
Check the box for Filter chromatic shift spots.
Type jS_Name = kitLoadJobset in MATLAB to load the jobset if it is not visible after reopening MATLAB.
Navigate to the raw data window and select the jobset saved with the chosen name.
Click Open to load the jobset into the Workspace window.
Spot quality control and kinetochore sister pairing in the CS channel.
Zoom in on the spot under consideration in the xy plane and projection of z slices.
Mark suggested spots within a 2.5 mm radius from the kinetochore spot with green crosses.
Identify previously ignored spots within a 2.5 mm radius and mark them with yellow crosses.
Indicate previously paired spots within a 2.5 mm radius with red crosses.
Press Space to exclude a distorted kinetochore spot or one with an undetected center.
Press on the respective green cross to pair two correctly recognized kinetochore spots.
Repeat steps for all cells to complete cell selection, manual sister pairing, and kinetochore spot quality control in the CS channel.
Kinetochore spot quality control in one NCS channel for Delta measurements.
Classify spots with non-Gaussian shape as ‘‘bad’’ spots.
Classify spots with wrong center detection as ‘‘bad’’ spots.
Use CS channel (CenpC-A561) for primary spot detection.
Explore Channel3 (Ndc80(N)-647) for spot quality assessment.
Create a movieStructure (mS).
Type mS_Name = kitLoadAllJobs(jS_Name) in the Command window to load analysis from the jobset into the movie structure.
Name the mS structure as specified: mS_expN_DateOfImaging_ProteinsInChannelOrder_Treatment.
Save the movieStructure in the folder with raw data.
Right-click on the mS structure and select Save as from the context menu.
Type the name of the mS structure in the “Save as” field.
Navigate to the folder with raw data and press Save.
Create a vector denoting the cells that have been selected for analysis.
Name the vector as specified: SelectedCells_expN_DateOfImaging_ProteinsInChannelOrder_Treatment.
Enter the index numbers of the selected cells in square brackets after the vector name in the Command window.
Save the SelectedCells vector in the folder with raw data using the Save as method.
Create a mS structure that contains only the cells selected for analysis.
Type in the Command window: mS_Name_sel = mS_Name(SelectedCells_Name).
Name the structure as suggested, ending with _sel: mS_expN_DateOfImaging_ProteinsInChannelOrder_Treatment_sel.
Save the mS_Name_sel using the chosen name from step 6e.
Create a spot selection structure (sS) in one NCS channel.
Type in the Command window: sS_Name_sel = kitSelectData(mS_Name_sel, ‘channel’, x, ‘method’, ‘deselect’).
If the function is terminated by pressing Command and C simultaneously, repeat step g from the beginning.
Discard non-Gaussian shaped asymmetric spots.
Discard spots with poor center detection.
Evaluate spot shape and center detection.
Ignore expanded or distorted spots.
Ignore spots when the cross marking is not in the center.
Input the relevant spots by typing in the Command window: [index numbers of spots to be ignored/selected].
Update metadata in the list of selected spots (sS_sel structure, created in g.) such that cell numbers correspond to raw image cell numbers.
In the Command window type: sS_Name = kitUpdateSpotSelections(sS_Name_sel, mS_Name, SelectedCells_Name).
Inspect spots in the second NCS channel and make a list of the “good”/”bad” spots.
Take into account the NCS channel previously analyzed for spot quality control.
Load the mS structure saved in step 6b if MATLAB has been closed and re-opened.
In the Command window type: sS_Name_sel = kitSelectData(mS_Name_sel, 'channel', x, 'method', 'deselect').
Choose an NCS channel different from the one analyzed in step 6.
Name the structure as indicated but also indicate the second NCS channel.
KiDv1.0.1 will prompt a window to save the sS structure file.
Navigate to the folder containing the raw images and press Save.
Identify kinetochores to discard in the second NCS channel.
Mark the respective indexes in the table made in step 6 g iii.
In the Command window, input the “Spots to be ignored”.
Type [indexes of spots to be discarded] in brackets for bad spots indexes in the first analyzed NCS channel and any additional identified bad spots.
If no spots are to be discarded, type [].

For example: In cell 1, if spots 3, 7, and 8 were initially ignored because of their signal in Channel 3 (Ndc80(N)-647), but spots 3, 4, and 5 were classified as bad spots in Channel 1 (Nnf1-A488), the new list will be [3 7 8 4 5].
Repeat steps until KiDv1.0.1 displays “Data selection complete”.
Update metadata in the list of selected spots such that cell numbers correspond to raw image cell numbers.
In the Command window type: sS_Name = kitUpdateSpotSelections(sS_Name_sel, mS_Name, SelectedCells_Name).

For example: sS_exp1_Nnf1CenpCNdc80N_DMSO_SpotsNdc80NNnf1 = kitUpdateSpotSelections(sS_exp1_Nnf1CenpCNdc80N_DMSO_SpotsNdc80NNnf1_sel, mS_exp1_15042020_Nnf1CenpCNdc80N_DMSO, SelectedCells_exp1_15042020_Nnf1CenpCNdc80N_DMSO)
Categorize kinetochores as ‘positive’ in the presence of the marker and ‘negative’ when the marker is absent.
Analyze categories by eye to measure Delta distance between non-categorized fluorescent channels at kinetochore marker positive and negative kinetochores.
In the Command window, type sS_Name_sel = kitSelectData(mS_Name_sel, ‘channel’, x, ‘method’, ‘select’).
Save the sS structure file in the folder containing raw images with the name specified.
Mark indexes of spots categorized as “positive” in the table made at steps 6g iii.
Type the indexes of spots to be selected in the Command window.
Include only those spots categorized as ‘‘positive’’ within the good (selected) spots at step 6g.
If no spots are to be selected, type [].
Repeat steps until KiDv1.0.1 displays “Data selection complete.”
In the Command window, type: sS_Name_sel = kitSelectData(mS_Name_sel, ‘channel’, x, ‘method’, ‘select’).
On the left is the name of the spot selection and x is the channel used to categorize kinetochores as negative.
If the function is terminated by pressing Command and C simultaneously, repeat step b from the beginning.
Identify the spots that can be categorized as “negative”.
Mark indexes of negative spots in the column of “good” (selected) spots in the table.
Input the ‘‘Spots to be selected’’ with the list of negative spot indexes, such as [4 5 9 10].
Repeat steps iii. and iv. until KiDv1.0.1 displays "Data selection complete" in the command window.
Update metadata in list of selected spots such that cell numbers correspond to raw image cell numbers.
In the Command window type: sS_Name = kitUpdateSpotSelections(sS_Name_sel, mS_Name, SelectedCells_Name).
Name the updated spot selection as the one created in step a. but omitting _sel: sS_expN_ProteinsInChannelOrder_Treatment_SpotsChannelMarkerP.
Update the list of Marker ‘negative’ kinetochores by typing the command: sS_Name = kitUpdateSpotSelections(sS_Name_sel, mS_Name, SelectedCells_Name).
Save the updated spot selection structure as described for the marker structure but with a name chosen in step 8c i. and ii.
Name the update spot selection without the _sel suffix, such as: sS_expN_ProteinsInChannelOrder_Treatment_SpotsChannelMarkerN
Continue to one of the following steps based on desired analysis:
Proceed to step 10 for analyzing intra-kinetochore Delta between two fluorescently labeled kinetochore markers at kinetochores ‘‘positive’’ and ‘‘negative’’ for a third marker.
Perform step 9, then proceed to step 10 for pooling data from biological replicates and Intra-kinetochore Delta measurements.
Proceed to step 11 for intensity measurements.
Pool data of experiments with biological replicates for kinetochore intra-measurements.
Ensure at least 300 kinetochores are available for BEDCA correction algorithm, using multiple biological replicates if necessary.
Pool the sS structures by typing the following command: sS_Pool_Name = kitCombineSpotSelections({sS_Name, sS_Name, sS_Name}).
Load the sS structures from the raw data folder into the Workspace window if they do not appear.
Rename the loaded variable to the name under which the sS structure was saved by typing in the Command Window: sS_Name = spotSelection.
Measure Delta in the Command window by typing: iM_Name = dublIntraMeasurements(mS_Name, ‘centralise’, 1, ‘channels’, [a b], ‘spotSelection’, sS_Name).
Include the treatment name flanked by underscores in the intra-kinetochore measurements variable name.
If no treatment is applied, use “_untreated_” for annotation.
Measure Delta using two channels from the sS list in step 6.
Measure Delta using three channels for each combination from the sS list in step 7.
Select channel combinations [1 2] and measure Delta.
Select channel combinations [2 3] and measure Delta.
Select channel combinations [1 3] and measure Delta.
Prepare sS lists as specified for step 8.
Perform dublIntraMeasurements using mS_exp1_2004202_Mad2CenpCNdc80N_DMSO with centralisation set to 1, channels [1 2], and spotSelection sS_exp1_Mad2CenpCNdc80N_DMSO_SpotsNdc80NMad2P.
Perform dublIntraMeasurements using mS_exp1_2004202_Mad2CenpCNdc80N_DMSO with centralisation set to 1, channels [1 2], and spotSelection sS_exp1_Mad2CenpCNdc80N_DMSO_SpotsNdc80NMad2N.
Generate quick statistics for the non-inflation corrected Delta measurements using dublBasicStats(iM_Name).
Display a list of characteristics in the Command window and choose the desired measurement by typing its number.
Plot kinetochore pair statistics using dublBasicPlots(iM_Name) and select the desired characteristic from the displayed list.
Access the non-inflation corrected Delta and kinetochore pair data saved in the iM structures.
Use .coords to access the detected kinetochore positions and distances.
Follow with .x, .y, or .z for the corresponding dimension of coordinates.
To filter out Delta>200nm, use iM_Name.microscope.depthFilter.delta.oneD for 1D measurements.
For 2D measurement vector with Delta>200nm filtered out, type iM_Name.microscope.depthFilter.delta.twoD.all.
Access the 3D measurement vector with Delta>200nm filtered out by typing iM_Name.microscope.depthFilter.delta.threeD.all.
To access raw Delta 1D measurements, use iM_Name.raw.microscope.delta.oneD.
For raw Delta 2D measurements, type iM_Name.raw.microscope.delta.twoD.all.
In the Command window type: IntiM_Name = dublIntensityMeasurements(mS_Name, ‘channels’, [a b], ‘paired’, 0 or 1, ‘refMarker’, ‘option’, ‘spotSelection’, sS_Name).
Note the suggested naming convention for intensity measurement as IntiM_expN_ProteinsInChannelOrder_Treatment_Marker1Marker2.
Set channels a and b in the function to specify which channels KiDv1.0.1 will measure intensity from, for example 'channels', [1 2].
Use 'paired', 1 to prompt kit to use only the kinetochores paired in step 5.
Use 'refMarker', 'self' to measure the intensity of the indicated channels in a mask centered at the detected kinetochore center.
Define the mask as a sphere with a radius of 300 nm, see step 4 d iii for details.
Use 'refMarker', 'inner' or 'outer' to specify using spot centers detected either in the inner or outer channel based on user-defined order (step 4 f. iii).
Measure intensity of Nnf1 around kinetochores detected in CenpC channel, using 'refMarker', 'inner'.
Measure intensity of CenpC around kinetochores detected in Nnf1 channel, using 'refMarker', 'outer'.
Measure CenpC intensity at kinetochores detected in the CenpC channel using ‘refMarker’, ‘self’.
Use a sphere with a 300 nm radius centered at the detected spot centers of CenpC kinetochores for measurement.
If measuring a selection of kinetochores made in the ‘Spot quality control’ section, state the sS list instead of sS_Name.
Otherwise, use an empty vector [] for sS_Name.
Access intensity measurements from IntiM structures created in step 11a.
Input 3D delta information from step 10 into the BEDCA algorithm.
Load iM structures saved in step 10 into MATLAB by dragging them to the Workspace window.
Select all treatments that correspond to the same experiment and protein-protein distance using Command + left mouse button click in the Workspace window.

Save the selected structure selection in one file in the MATLAB/BEDCA/ExptData directory with a name that excludes treatment annotation but includes the individual iM structures' names, ensuring they are of the same distance and experiment but different treatments.
Input the single file into BEDCA as described above.
Access each treatment in BEDCA using the ‘treatment’ input in the Run_BEDCA function.
Click with the right mouse button on the iM structure in the Workspace window.
Select Save as from the context menu.
Type the name of the iM structure without Treatment annotation for saving.
Choose MATLAB/BEDCA/ExptData as the directory for saving.
Repeat the process for all iM structures to be corrected, including all protein-protein distance measurements.

Indicate the iM file name saved in the ExptData folder that will be used for correction.

Check that the a parameter is set to 4 as default.
Try a smaller a, such as a=1 if necessary.
Evaluate spot center accuracy using mean taux and tauz estimates.
Verify correct annotation of staining in the ExptData_list file.
Optimize imaging conditions for improved signal-to-noise ratio if issues persist.

Pool the data before running BEDCA correction as described in step 9 above.
Evaluate the quality of the BEDCA run to ensure informative results.
Evaluate the posterior Distribution.

Evaluate convergence using GRc values.
